subject: [PATCH 4/6] daxctl: report whole-device hotplug state in 'daxctl list'

2026-10-16.patch_summary: This patch modifies the 'daxctl list' command to report the whole-device hotplug state as a new field called 'hotplug_state'. The kernel's daxX.Y/state attribute only updates when written, so it can become stale if blocks are toggled individually. To address this issue, the patch introduces a function called 'hotplug_state' that returns a string indicating whether the device is in an inconsistent state or not. If the device is consistent, the function returns a string describing its hotplug state based on its current online and movable memory status.

reviews.author: Alison Schofield
reviews.summary: The patch has been reviewed and found to be acceptable. Alison provided a Reviewed-by tag indicating her approval of the patch.
reviews.raw_body:
On Fri, Oct 16, 2026 at 05:42:46PM -0400, Gregory Price (Meta) wrote:
> From: Gregory Price <gourry@gourry.net>
> 
> Report daxX.Y/state as 'hotplug_state' in 'daxctl list'. The kernel
> only updates it when written, so it goes stale if blocks are toggled
> individually. Report 'inconsistent' when the blocks' online state or
> zone disagrees with it; online_memblocks, total_memblocks and movable
> show the actual state.
> 
> The attribute only appears when daxX.Y/state exists, so output on
> older kernels is unchanged. ('state' already reports 'disabled'.)


Reviewed-by: Alison Schofield <alison.schofield@intel.com>

2026-10-21.patch_summary: This patch series updates the daxctl tool to report whole-device hotplug state in 'daxctl list'. The kernel's daxX.Y/state attribute only changes when written, so it can become stale if blocks are toggled individually. To address this, the patch introduces a new function, hotplug_state(), which returns the actual state of the device based on its online and zone information.
